prompt_text: What is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City MO for someone who is self-employed?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single “best” broker for everyone — the right one depends on your needs (budget, preferred carriers, whether you want ACA marketplace plans, HSA-qualified plans, dental/vision, in‑person help, etc.). I can find and recommend local brokers, but first a few quick questions to narrow it down:

- Are you shopping for an individual/ family ACA plan, short‑term coverage, or something else (e.g., COBRA, dental, supplemental)?
- Do you want someone local you can meet in person in Kansas City, MO, or is phone/online help fine?
- Any must‑have features (specific doctors/hospitals, HSA eligibility, low deductible, budget)?
- Your ZIP code (optional) so I can pull nearby brokers.

If you want to start right away, here’s how to choose a good broker and some steps you can take:

What to look for in a broker
- Independent vs captive: independent brokers can compare many carriers; captive agents represent one company. For self‑employed people who want choice, independents are often better.  
- ACA/individual market experience: confirm they regularly enroll clients in Marketplace plans if you need subsidies or special enrollment.  
- Credentials: NAHU membership or state insurance license. Ask to see their license number.  
- Fees and compensation: many individual plan brokers are paid by carriers (no direct charge to you), but ask up front if they charge a fee.  
- Availability and service: will they help after you enroll (claims, renewals, mid‑year changes)?  
- Reviews and references: check Google/BBB and ask for references of self‑employed clients.

Questions to ask a broker
- Which carriers and plan types do you commonly work with in Kansas City, MO?
- Do you help with ACA Marketplace enrollments and subsidy eligibility?
- How do you get paid? Will I owe you any fees?
- Can you help with claim issues or changes after enrollment?
- How many clients like me (self‑employed) do you serve?

Places to find reputable brokers in Kansas City
- HealthCare.gov’s “Find Local Help” tool (for Marketplace agents/navigators)  
- National Association of Health Underwriters (NAHU) “Find an Agent”  
- Local Google/BBB reviews for “independent health insurance agent Kansas City MO”

If you want, give me your ZIP code and preferences and I’ll find and compare 3–5 local independent brokers/agents who specialize in individual/ self‑employed plans and summarize reviews, services, and how to contact them. Which would you prefer?
